$provenance: AUTHORED IN THIS REPO. Not from tether-design.zip. Not clinically reviewed.
$comment: The eight non-shell screens of supplement.product.preventive.json. SH1–SH6 are the host shell and are not authored here. The person throughout is Marisol Reyes, 42, who works three nights a week, has two children, had a flu shot at the Grand Avenue Pharmacy on 14 October 2025 and a cervical screening in March 2023, has a dental cleaning booked for 4 November 2026, and lives with Julián. Every string is unreviewed. The review dates in the learn library are illustrative: nothing in this repository has been through clinical review.

S01.headline: The checks you keep meaning to book.
S01.sub: Groundwork holds the dates — what you have had, when you were told to come back, and a quiet reminder near the time. It does not decide what you need. It remembers what you told it.

blocks.title: It remembers, it doesn't decide
blocks.body: Every date here is one you typed, or copied off a letter. Groundwork never works out what you are owed, or when.

blocks.title: Nothing on your lock screen
blocks.body: A reminder says “Groundwork”. Not which check, not which part of you, not why.

blocks.title: Yours to take away
blocks.body: Export the whole record as one page, or delete it outright. Deletion is finished, not hidden.

S01.footer: Education and reminders. Not a diagnosis, not a screening test, and not a substitute for a clinician. English only so far.

S02.title: What it does
S02.headline: Four moments this is built for.
S02.sub: Not four features. Four ways a date gets lost.

blocks.title: When the card goes in a drawer
blocks.body: A clinic says “three years”. Three years is a long time to keep a piece of card. Type it once and it is still here when the three years are up.

blocks.title: When you are at the pharmacy anyway
blocks.body: The flu shot in the autumn, and the record of it thirty seconds later, before the receipt goes through the wash.

blocks.title: When the reminder lands while you are at work
blocks.body: It says “Groundwork” and nothing else. Anybody reading over your shoulder learns the name of an app.

blocks.title: When a new practice asks what you have had
blocks.body: One page, in date order, that you can hand over or read off your phone while they type.

blocks.title: What it isn't
blocks.body: It does not tell you what you need, whether a check is covered, or whether a gap matters. It has no idea what your clinician already knows, and it is not a way of avoiding asking them.

S02.footer: Education and reminders. Not a diagnosis or a screening test.

S03.title: Consent & privacy
S03.headline: What we hold, and what we don't.

blocks.title: Held on your phone
blocks.body: The dates you enter, the words you enter them with, and the reminders you set. These stay on this device.

blocks.title: Shared with a clinic
blocks.body: Nothing, ever, on its own. There is no practice, pharmacy or insurer connected to Groundwork. If a clinic wants your record, you export it and hand it over.

blocks.title: Never asked for
blocks.body: No insurance details, no member number, no results, no numbers off a test. Groundwork stores dates and the words you used. A blood pressure reading has a home, and it is not here — it is with whoever can do something about it.

blocks.title: You can leave with everything
blocks.body: Export as a readable page plus a structured file, or delete the lot. Deletion is completed on this phone and anywhere it synced — not hidden from the list.

items.title: I understand and agree
items.body: Groundwork records dates I enter. It does not decide which checks apply to me.

items.title: Remind me near a date I have entered
items.body: Generic wording only. You can change it or switch it off in Settings, and nobody else is told.

actions.label: See what leaving looks like first

S03.footer: The second choice is optional and reversible. The first is how the app works, and there is no version of it that shares more.

S04.title: Today
S04.headline: Good evening, Marisol.
S04.sub: One date coming up, and nothing you have to do about it tonight.

blocks.title: Get help now
blocks.body: Reachable from every screen, in every programme.

blocks.title: Flu shot · you wrote “each autumn”
blocks.body: The last one was 14 October 2025, at the pharmacy on Grand Avenue. You asked for a reminder on 1 October.

blocks.eyebrow: Why there is no score up there
blocks.body: No percentage complete, no gaps found, no green tick. A score would mean Groundwork had decided which checks belong on your list. It has not, and it will not. The list is the one you typed.

blocks.title: Not sure whether something can wait?
blocks.body: This app cannot tell you. Your practice can, and there is a line that takes general questions in English and Spanish.

blocks.title: Add something you have had done
blocks.body: Thirty seconds. A name, a date, and who told you when to come back.

blocks.title: Grand Avenue Pharmacy
blocks.body: The number you entered, off the sign you photographed. Walk-in flu shots, it said.

S04.footer: Works offline · Nothing on this screen has left your phone

S05.title: Your record
S05.headline: What you have had, and what you wrote down next.
S05.sub: Seven rows, all typed by you or copied off a letter. Groundwork worked none of them out.

blocks.title: Coming up
blocks.body: Dates you entered, in the words you entered them with.

items: “Each autumn” · you set a reminder for 1 October
“Come back in three years” · you wrote March 2026
Booked 4 November, 8:00 am · you entered this on 3 September

blocks.title: About that March row
blocks.body: You wrote March 2026, and it is September. Groundwork is not calling that late. We do not know whether you have been since, whether it was moved, or what your clinic has already decided — so the row says what you typed and nothing more. Change it, or ask them. Either beats a guess from us.

items: 2017 · you were not sure of the month, so we left it off
May 2026 · the date only. The number went to your practice, not here.

blocks.title: Add a check
blocks.value: Eye test — Julián says every two years

blocks.title: A date is not a verdict
blocks.body: Nothing on this screen means a check applies to you, and nothing on it means you are covered. Groundwork does not know your history, your pregnancies, your family, what you can afford, or what a clinician has already ruled out. A reminder you set for yourself is not an entitlement and not a clinical opinion. It is an alarm clock in your own handwriting.

blocks.title: This record belongs to one person
blocks.body: You. Not the children, not your mother. A second person needs their own record, because two sets of rows in one list makes it unclear whose body a row is about — and that is the kind of mistake that ends up in a consulting room.

blocks.title: Take it away
blocks.body: One readable page in date order, plus a structured file. Hand it to a new practice, or just keep it. It stays on your phone until you send it.

blocks.title: Or delete it
blocks.body: Any single row, or the whole record. Deletion is completed on this phone, on our servers and in anything queued to sync. It is not hidden from the list and kept behind it.

S05.footer: Saves offline · Every row is editable and every row is deletable, including the ones we imported from nowhere, which is all of them

S06.title: Learn
S06.headline: Why a check exists, in plain language.
S06.sub: Six pieces and one table. Each shows who published it and when.

blocks.title: What a screening programme is actually for
blocks.body: 5 min · reviewed August 2026

items: WHY THE FLU VACCINE IS A YEARLY ONE
WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENS AT A ROUTINE CHECKUP
WHY GUIDANCE CHANGES, AND WHY THAT IS NOT A SCANDAL
ASKING WHAT SOMETHING WILL COST BEFORE YOU GO
WHAT TO DO WITH A LETTER YOU DO NOT UNDERSTAND

blocks.eyebrow: Published guidance, quoted and not applied
blocks.title: Who says what, and in which year
blocks.body: Reproduced with the body that issued it and the year it was issued. Every line describes a population. Whether it describes you is a question for somebody with your history in front of them.

items: A flu vaccine every season for everyone aged 6 months and over, with few exceptions
A Td or Tdap booster every 10 years
Screening for high blood pressure in adults aged 18 and over
Ages 21 to 65, by one of several methods and intervals
Mammography every two years, ages 40 to 74

blocks.title: We show all of it, not the part that fits you
blocks.body: Groundwork could filter this table down to an age you typed in. It does not. Deciding which rows apply to a person is a screening judgment, and this app does not make one — it would be wrong often enough to matter, and you would have no way of telling when. Read the lot, and take what looks relevant to somebody who can say.

blocks.title: Why the dates are on the front
blocks.body: The breast row moved in 2024 and the colorectal row moved in 2021. Anything here that has not been rechecked in eighteen months comes down rather than sitting there looking current.

blocks.title: If something needs an answer today
blocks.body: There is a line that takes general questions about vaccines and preventive care, in English and Spanish. Anything about your own body belongs with your practice.

S06.footer: Nothing here recommends a test, a vaccine or a course of treatment, and nothing here knows your history.

S07.title: Support
S07.headline: A route to a person.
S07.sub: Nothing is sent until you have read it and pressed send.

blocks.title: In an emergency
blocks.body: If you are in danger, or thinking about harming yourself, call 911 or your local emergency number now.

blocks.title: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
blocks.body: Call or text 988 · English and Spanish · 24 hours.

blocks.title: CDC-INFO
blocks.body: English and Spanish. General questions about vaccines and preventive care. They have no access to your record, and neither do we.

items: The number you entered · they hold your history, we don't
Walk-in flu shots · the number you entered
“Can you take the kids on Thursday morning?”

blocks.title: There is no coach in this programme
blocks.body: Some Tether programmes have one. This one does not. A reminder list with a coach bolted on would be a clinic pretending to be an app, and the thing standing between you and a dental appointment is usually a Thursday morning rather than advice.

blocks.title: If you do send something
blocks.body: You read the exact page first: your dates and the words you used, nothing else, and no interpretation attached, because there is not one to attach.

actions.label: See what a share would contain

S07.footer: Crisis numbers route to United States services.

S08.title: Settings & privacy

blocks.title: Notifications
blocks.body: Detail is off, and this programme ships that way. A reminder says “Groundwork” and nothing else — not which check, not which part of you, not the date. Anyone who sees your lock screen learns the name of an app, which is the most a lock screen should ever give away.

blocks.title: Reminders you have set
blocks.body: One, for 1 October at 09:00. It says “Groundwork”, it does not repeat, and you set it. We did not work out that you needed it.

items: 7 · every one editable, every one deletable
Nothing shared · no clinic is connected
English · Spanish is not written yet
Nothing, unless you export it and send it

blocks.title: Export everything
blocks.body: A readable page and a structured file: your dates, the words you used, and the reminders you set. It stays on your phone unless you send it.

blocks.title: Delete everything
blocks.body: Completed, not hidden — this phone, our servers, and anything queued to sync. It cannot be undone, and it ends this programme.

Education and reminders. Groundwork does not screen, diagnose, treat or prescribe, it does not decide which checks apply to you, and it is not a substitute for advice from a qualified health professional.

S08.footer: Turning detail on takes effect straight away. So does turning it off.
